Services

WordPress to Webflow Migration Agency

A WordPress to Webflow migration rebuilds your site for visual editing and managed hosting. We map content and URLs, review plugin replacements, test the new site and track search performance through launch. Your team rehearses its publishing tasks before handover.

Get in touch
Migration planning

How do you migrate from WordPress to Webflow safely?

Start with a URL and content inventory, preserve useful URLs and metadata, map changed addresses to relevant destinations, and test redirects, forms and analytics before launch. Keep a recoverable copy of the old site. After cutover, check indexing, traffic and enquiries against the dated baseline.

Migrated Properly

What Moving Off WordPress Gives Marketing

The ProblemStandard Agency

The campaign page waits on a PHP developer

Custom PHP and a tangle of plugins mean every real change waits on the one developer who understands how the site was built. The campaign window closes while the request sits in the queue.

A plugin update takes the site down on launch day

Every feature is another third-party plugin, and every update is a chance something else breaks. The site needs constant patching to stay safe, and someone has to own that cycle for as long as it runs.

The move itself is the risk nobody prices

Most migration damage is self-inflicted: URLs bulk-redirected to the home page, a thousand words cut to fit a tidier template, schema left behind. The rankings fall two months later, and by then the old site is gone.

The SolutionThe Legency Approach

The rankings you earned come with you

Every URL with traffic, backlinks or conversions is inventoried before anything is designed, mapped one to one, and monitored through cutover. When K2 Group retired a legacy domain, all 261 stranded URLs were mapped to new homes.

Your team publishes without a developer

The plugin stack is replaced by native Webflow features and a governed component library. A new landing page or case study assembles from parts that already match, on marketing’s calendar.

The patching liability ends at cutover

Hosting, CDN, SSL and security updates become Webflow’s job. The plugin cycle ends, and with it the risk that one missed update makes the site a target.

What Stays Measurable

What You Can Still Prove After the Move

Rankings tracked through the switch

The old site stays live until the new one is proven, and rankings are tracked through the switch rather than checked after the fact. If a page moves, you know which one and why.

Before-and-after comparisons that hold

Goals, events and historical data carry over, so the first report after launch compares like with like instead of starting from a blank dashboard. The question of whether the migration hurt gets a numbered answer.

AI citations counted from launch day

The same monthly citation checks we run for every client start the day the new site goes live, so visibility in AI answers is measured from the first month rather than assumed.

Content and functionality

What moves from WordPress to Webflow?

The move from WordPress to Webflow includes content, templates and integrations. A content import transfers records; the website design and behaviour still need to be built and checked.

Posts, pages and media

Map fields to Webflow CMS collections, import a sample and check images, references and slugs. Confirm the plan's collection limits before the full import. Webflow's migration guide explains the XML-to-CSV content route.

Templates and plugin behaviour

Rebuild layouts as reusable components. Review forms, search, localisation and other plugin-dependent features separately, with a named replacement or an agreed reason to retain the current setup.

URLs and launch checks

Keep useful URLs where possible, redirect changed paths and check links, metadata, forms and analytics. Retain a recoverable copy of the old site and agree who can approve the cutover.

Choosing the direction

Considering a Webflow to WordPress migration?

The right direction depends on your requirements. WordPress may suit a site that depends on its plugin ecosystem or needs direct control of hosting and server code. Moving from Webflow to WordPress still needs a content model, redirect map, form and integration tests, and an agreed owner for maintenance. We assess platform fit before recommending a migration.

The Only Real Risk

A Migration Can Lose You Traffic You Spent Years Earning

The design is the easy half. What decides whether a migration is a success six months later is whether the search equity came across, and that is a mapping problem rather than a design one.

  1. 01

    Inventory before anything is designed

    Every URL with impressions, clicks, backlinks or conversions, pulled from Search Console and a full crawl. This is the document the whole migration is judged against, and it has to exist before the new site has a shape.

  2. 02

    A one-to-one redirect map

    Every old URL points at its closest equivalent. Bulk-redirecting to the home page is the standard shortcut, and it discards most of the equity the redirect was there to keep. Where no equivalent exists, that is a decision recorded rather than a 404 discovered later.

  3. 03

    Carry the words that earned the ranking

    A page that ranks does so because of what it says. Cutting a thousand words to fit a tidier template is the most common self-inflicted loss in a migration, and it is invisible until the rankings move.

  4. 04

    Metadata, schema and canonicals move too

    Titles, descriptions, structured data and canonical tags are part of what the old site earned. Rebuilding the page and leaving them behind is a rebuild that starts from zero on purpose.

  5. 05

    Watch it weekly for ninety days

    Crawl weekly against the pre-launch inventory and fix what moved. Most migration damage is cheap to reverse in the first month and expensive once a quarter has passed.

Straight Answers

The Trade You Are Making

What gets better

Marketing can publish without a developer. There is no plugin stack to patch and no plugin conflict to debug. Hosting, CDN and SSL stop being your problem. Most teams find the speed improvement arrives for free, because the thing that was slow was usually the plugins.

What you give up

The plugin ecosystem, which is the thing WordPress does best. If your site depends on a specific plugin doing something unusual, that has to be solved before a migration is agreed rather than discovered halfway through. We will tell you if it is a reason not to move.
